links.outcome: Performance on unseen modality-anatomy-task combinations versus seen combinations
links.effect: Related-split models reached 83.2% classification accuracy and 0.75 segmentation cIoU; performance dropped significantly under Unrelated and zero-overlap conditions.
links.quote: Models trained on Related splits achieve 83.2 percent classification accuracy and 0.75 segmentation cIoU, while performance drops significantly under Unrelated and zero-overlap conditions, demonstrating the benchmark difficulty.

unlisted_practices: Cross-task transfer training: segmentation cIoU improved by 7% when trained with classification-only data

screen.reason: The paper introduces CrossMed, a benchmark for evaluating compositional generalization in medical multimodal foundation models across combinations of modality, anatomy, and task, without evaluating clinical deployment practices.
